reviewer: Specialist B, atomic presentation and physical ownership
findings: Task index, function and borrowed context are acquired under the dispatch mutex as one current-generation claim.
Actual-task completion decreases only after the noexcept callback returns, under the same mutex used by the dispatch waiter. No callback/context access follows the completion edge.
A worker arriving late holds no previous context and can only claim a real task from the current dispatch. Idle workers do not grant or withhold task completion.
Nonzero overlapping and nested calls fail before replacing active dispatch storage; RAII release leaves subsequent valid dispatch possible.
Worker counts outside1..256 and a missing nonzero-work callback fail before worker admission or context mutation.
Constructor failure stops and joins the initialized worker prefix while synchronization members remain alive.
The all-worker control remains present; its context cannot retire until every awakened worker acknowledges.
limits: Exclusive external object lifetime remains required: concurrent destruction or use after destruction is not an admitted operation.
Completion statistics are owner-only; unsynchronized concurrent readers of non-atomic completed counters are not admitted.
A zero-task dispatch is an explicit no-op and grants no completion counters.
This is source cross-review, not an independent sanitizer rerun, full World proof, or performance adoption. Native Specialist A owns those recorded gates.
required_before_selection: Source-bound full World equal-step semantics and actual mounted native module
Normal and applicable sanitizer lifetime gates with leak-check limitations retained
Registered interleaved physical progression with actualtask exercise and resource/freshness assessment
